title: How can one rule give Ruhee's age from Ziva's age?
description: Ruhee is three years younger than Ziva. A rule with letters gives the younger age from the older age, and it is used when Ziva is twenty. Keeko doubts that the rule adds three.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one person is younger, the rule takes away from the older age, and the same letter rule fits every age. Watch for students who add three because the words say three years.

source: Ziva is 3 years older than Ruhee. Write an expression for Ruhee's age using s for Ziva's age
video_script.why: A learner sees that the same two people give a second rule, this time by taking away three from the older age.
video_script.substitution: The book's own question about Ziva and Ruhee, now asked the other way round, with the age twenty.
video_script.anchor: Ziva and Ruhee, whose ages are always three years apart
video_script.wrong_answer: the younger age is s plus three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds three to the older age because the question says three years, but the younger person has the smaller age; with s as ten the sum gives thirteen, which is older.

final_answer.spoken: the rule is eigh equals s minus three, and Ruhee is seventeen years old

never_show: the age 17 before the answer beat
maths_rules: Ruhee is 3 years younger, so the age of Ruhee is 3 less than the age of Ziva.
With s for the age of Ziva and a for the age of Ruhee: a = s - 3.
video_script.design: One idea: younger means less, so subtract. Assumes the idea of a letter standing for an age. The two names stay on the stage and the arrow between the ages is reversed. Wrong idea: add three to the older age.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; Ziva and Ruhee drawn side by side, with the words three years younger written under Ruhee

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: the two children appear with the words three years younger under Ruhee
marks.p3: a question mark glows over the age of Ruhee

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>Ruhee is three years younger than Ziva, and the book wants a rule for the age of Ruhee.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>The rule must start from the age of Ziva, whatever that age may be.
How can we write such a rule?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two age bars side by side, a long one for Ziva and a shorter one for Ruhee; the gap between the ends is marked 3 years

marks.g1: the longer bar for Ziva is drawn
marks.g2: the shorter bar for Ruhee is drawn beside it
marks.g3: the gap between the two ends is marked three years

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Here are the two ages as bars, the longer bar for Ziva.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The shorter bar is for Ruhee, who is the younger one.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The gap between the two bars is always three years.

beats.on_screen: Given: Ziva is 3 years older than Ruhee; s = age of Ziva, a = age of Ruhee

marks.gv1: the first fact is written on the working board
marks.gv2: the letters s and a are written beside the two names

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, Ziva is three years older than Ruhee.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Let s stand for the age of Ziva, and eigh for the age of Ruhee.

beats.on_screen: To find: a rule for a using s; the age of Ruhee when Ziva is 20

marks.fd2: the second aim is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find a rule that gives eigh from s.
<bookmark mark='fd2'/>Then we find the age of Ruhee when Ziva is twenty.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: Ruhee is younger, so the age of Ruhee is 3 less than s

marks.s1a: the shorter bar is shown three years shorter than the longer bar
marks.s1b: the words 3 less than s are written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Ruhee is three years younger, so the age of Ruhee is smaller.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>It is three less than the age of Ziva.

marks.s2a: the words 3 less than s change into s − 3

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Three less than s is written s minus three.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>The rule is eigh equals s minus three, for every age of Ziva.

marks.s3a: s is replaced by 20 in the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>To use the rule, replace s by twenty.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Then eigh equals twenty minus three.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a = s − 3, and a = 17 years

marks.ans: 17 years is boxed beside the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ruhee is seventeen years old when Ziva is twenty.
The rule for every age is eigh equals s minus three.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the younger age is s + 3, struck out; the two bars come back with s as 10 and the sum 13 drawn longer than the older bar

marks.d2: the two bars come back with the older bar at ten

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks the younger age is s plus three, since the question says three years.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Try s as ten, and that rule gives thirteen for the younger one.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>That is more than the older age, so the rule must take three away, not add it.
